summary: Baileys fork with import-time call-home and unpinned author-controlled `libsignal` alias
details: This is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. On every `require('@alannxd/baileys')`, the package's main entry (`lib/index.js`) performs an unconditional HTTPS GET to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information.json` on a mutable branch of the author's personal GitHub repo and prints one string from the response via `console.log`. The response body is only logged — it is not passed to `eval`/`exec`/`Function`/`require` — so this is a covert usage phone-home (leaks installer IP + User-Agent + import-time signal to the author on each load) rather than a remote-code-execution channel. Separately, `package.json` declares `"libsignal": "npm:@alannxd/libsignal-node@latest"`, aliasing the well-known `libsignal` import specifier to an author-scoped package tracked at `latest`; every `require('libsignal')` inside this package resolves to whatever the author currently publishes there, giving the author a persistent mutable code channel into consumers' dependency trees. The `ping` and `child_process`/HTTP patterns matched by pattern rules resolve to Baileys' normal media-upload and connectivity code paths (POST/GET against WhatsApp media endpoints), not to attacker infrastructure. No credential harvesting, no environment scraping, no filesystem enumeration, and no exfiltration of caller data were observed in the traced code. Concerns are undisclosed import-time beacon to author-controlled mutable infrastructure and an unpinned author-controlled alias overriding a well-known module name — both consent/transparency issues warranting human review of maintainer trust before recommending this fork.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
